fixtures.title: Callback envelope admission, extended data and the elevated load series
fixtures.scenario: Sections 18.1-18.2: known metadata, an unknown schema with opaque bytes, known content under a metadata-only policy, header-only evidence, allowlisted and denied extended items, and a real EVENT_RECORD extended-data array read in bounded copies. The harness then drives a declared load series through both evidence variants, so the bounded queue reaches its limit and the writer becomes the pacing stage. The journal variant writes journal-v1; the format itself is FX-JOURNAL-002.

truth.independence: The corpus declares original bytes and policy inputs before admission; expected dispositions are stored separately.

expected.note: All four headers remain attributable. Only approved metadata survives; unknown and content bodies and a denied extended item have explicit omission outcomes; and an over-long extended item keeps its original length.

environment.result: Four five-level elevated series on a supported build: two writing the disposable probe format, on whose evidence ADR-008 was accepted, and two writing journal-v1 after the capture path moved to it. The journal-v1 call-stack series reports decisionReady: true with no blockers: identical ordered replay and an unchanged source clock at every level, 77,355 of 77,355 extended items copied, persisted and replayed, the queue bound reached with 60,006 counted drops and zero loss, and the writer pacing at 128% of an acquisition window in the clean series. journal-v1 costs 231 bytes per admitted record against the probe format's 327.

The portable admission policy round-trips admitted identity and extended items, excludes unapproved bodies and denied extended types, and rejects checksum corruption. The extended-data walker is asserted against a synthetic EVENT_RECORD, not against a live capture. The load series, its saturation classifier and the storage probe arithmetic are asserted portably; the elevated runs they describe are recorded under bench/results/.

provenance.contents: Synthetic headers, schemas, content markers, extended items, a synthetic EVENT_RECORD layout and expected policy dispositions.

fixtures.title: The frozen journal-v1 framing and its buffer ownership

fixtures.title: The canonical query identity of a metric specification
fixtures.scenario: Sections 10.4 and 10.5: fourteen metric specifications over a fixed snapshot, each written in canonical form and hashed. They cover a whole-capture count, an interval, an implied domain, layer and side, a rate, a grouping whose evidence policy cannot matter, a ranked grouping whose rows sit beside the hash, an executable grouping with candidates, and owner, participant-by-peer and sender-with-peer focus, a between filter written from the first set to the second, and a channel count that names the binding rule and no policy.

truth.independence: Every request and snapshot value is fixed in the test, and every hash can be recomputed from its canonical line with any SHA-256 implementation.

expected.note: The corpus is the contract: name, identity token and canonical specification per line. A change to it is a new canonicalization version or an ADR, never a test update.

environment.result: All fourteen lines reproduce byte for byte and their hashes match an independent SHA-256. Implicit and written-out defaults hash alike, a policy that cannot change an answer is dropped, requested rows share a hash, and every member, snapshot, role and peer difference is a different identity. Answers carry the identity of their generation, unavailable answers included. A between filter has one spelling per meaning: either order of an undirected pair, a backward direction and its forward spelling, and a repeated instance all hash alike.

provenance.contents: Synthetic identities and a fixed manifest digest. Nothing captured.

fixtures.title: WinINet exchanges at once in one process, with chunked responses
fixtures.scenario: Several exchanges at once and chunked responses (ADR-037, revision 244): eight WinINet clients in one process, each on its own connection handle and taking every eighth of 256 requests, post to the loopback server, which answers in chunked transfer coding with seeded chunks of 1 to 9,000 bytes; WinINet's capture provider is enabled for the workload's process alone.

truth.independence: The loopback server is the witness: it logs every request head and body it received and every response head it sent, and each response body twice - the body a client reads and the framed bytes the wire carried - by length and SHA-256, never the bytes. Tier ExperimentalEvidence: HTTP/2, compressed responses and asynchronous WinINet are unmeasured (ADR-037).

environment.result: Recorded by icat record --profile content scoped to the workload's process: 2,331 records delivered and journaled, 4,406,997 bytes of content kept, nothing lost.
